correctness.rationale: For finite nonempty P with n elements and m comparable ordered pairs x<y over F_q, every commuting family of idempotents is simultaneously conjugate by a unique u in U=1+J into Boolean diagonal idempotents D. The orthogonal joint idempotent projectors p_sigma and u=sum p_sigma d_sigma have diagonal 1 and prove existence. The centralizer of all diagonal primitive idempotents within idempotents is D, establishing maximality and unique U indexing, |U|=q^m. For relative g=u^-1 v, diagonal bits commute iff constant on components of the support graph H_g; intersection size is 2^{c(H_g)}. Every strict interval coordinate of uniform g independently vanishes with probability 1/q, giving q^-m sum_B(q-1)^|B|t^{c(B)} and its FK/Tutte transform. Infinitely many prime powers permit interpolation; min-cut events give b_lambda q^-lambda+O(q^-lambda-1). Independently enumerated every unipotent conjugate and actual idempotent overlaps for the n=3 F2 chain, finding eight semilattices and histogram {2:4,4:3,8:1}; finite check corroborates structural proof.

originality.rationale: Classical incidence-monoid work characterizes individual idempotents and their conjugacy classes, and the Fortuin–Kasteleyn identity itself is classical. The new claim is the precise distribution of pairwise intersections of all maximal commuting-idempotent semilattices, with graph-completeness and min-cut asymptotics. This does not follow from individual-idempotent enumeration without the simultaneous diagonalizer and support-intersection lemma.
residual_risks: An older general theorem on intersections of conjugate diagonal Boolean algebras may imply part of the census.
The Tutte transform is classical; claims of originality are limited to the incidence-monoid interpretation and associated distribution/reconstruction.
Finite F2 enumeration does not prove all posets and fields.
